Let me wrap up my thoughts into an easily digestible mass.

Logical is not grounded in some hypothetical deity. It is grounded in its usefulness to those who apply it. You don't need to add God to Newton's equations to get to the moon. You just need carefully constructed experiment and independent verification. This method can by no means lead us to absolute certainty that our ideas are true, but it can determine that our ideas are true enough to be applied successfully to real-world problems, and that's all that really matters to us as human beings.

So when I question the existence of a personal and interested God, I am questioning its usefulness as an explanatory framework. I'm questioning its usefulness to solve real-world problems.
